messages:
anna_cs: FYI Riverbend reporting a sudden p99 jump on embeddings since ~04:05 UTC, started after a large campaign rollout. p95 ~240ms -> 800ms, p99 ~220ms -> 1.6s. customer pipeline is timing out. sample request IDs: r-0a1b2c3d, r-0a1b2c8f, r-0a1b2c99

anna_cs: reproducer from them: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -d '{"input": ["<very long doc>"], "model":"embed-large"}'` they see intermittent 5xx and long tails.

jess_support: got the ticket, asked for their traffic window and whether they're using batching. Omar said spike correlates with their nightly batch at 04:00 UTC. No changes on their side except more concurrent workers. :thinking_face:

mike_oncall: looking at infra graphs now. Noticing a cluster-wide KV cache miss rate up ~3x on region-us-east-1 at 04:02. Also a couple of embedding workers had CPU all-in bursts. Could be interleaving long-context requests adding memory pressure.

lee_eng: also noticing a single tenant (riverbend-tenant-id) accounts for ~68% of concurrent embeddings at that time. Their median token length jumped from 200 -> 7k tokens during the batch. That aligns with KV churn + eviction thrash.

mike_oncall: can we confirm if long contexts bypass prefix caching? If so lots of cold KV reads.

lee_eng: yes, our caching window is 4k tokens. Anything over that falls back to cold path. Their job concatenates many docs so most requests are >4k. Overflow causes more memory movement and occasional GC pauses in the embedding workers.

deploy-bot: deploy service/embeddings-runtime v2.3.1 started roll forward at 04:12 UTC on region-us-east-1 (watch: 3/5 nodes).

anna_cs: customer is asking for immediate mitigation — they can throttle if needed but want minimal impact to throughput.

jess_support: I suggested temporary concurrency limit on their API key + instructing them to shard requests into smaller docs. Omar asked if we can do anything server-side.

mike_oncall: short-term mitigations we can apply ASAP: 1) per-tenant concurrency cap (limit to 60 concurrent embedding requests) 2) soft-drop extremely long requests >12k tokens with 429 + Retry-After 10s 3) pin them to a reserved worker pool (1 slot) for isolation while we investigate. Any objections?

lee_eng: agree. Also recommend enabling aggressive KV prefetch for pinned pool (lower cache TTL but avoid evictions). Will need config patch to autoscaler to pin 1 slot.

anna_cs: please note customer asked for an allowlist so their batch can run without throttles next week. They'll consider reserved capacity but want trial.

mike_oncall: action plan: - apply per-tenant cap now (60) - add server-side long-request 429 rule for >12k tokens - create reserved slot and toggle prefetch TTL for that pool - follow up with perf graphs in 15m. I'll own changes.

lee_eng: starting the pin now, will also flip prefetch TTL to 30s for pinned pool.

mike_oncall: applied cap and 429 rule at 04:25 UTC. Monitoring latency...

anna_cs: told Omar we applied temporary cap + long-request guard, asked them to retry their batch in 10m and report results.

omar_cust: thanks team — will kick off a small-run now and report within 20m. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: reserved-slot allocation succeeded for tenant riverbend-tenant-id (slot_id rs-77).

lee_eng: early signs: p99 down from 1.6s -> ~420ms for region affected, KV miss rate trending down. Still a few tail blips but much better.

mike_oncall: logging follow-ups: collect stack traces for the remaining 5xxs and capture full request headers for the pinned slot. Also scheduling a postmortem if this repeats next week.

jess_support: will update ticket and ask Omar if they want a short trial of reserved capacity (1 slot) for next nightly run.

anna_cs: thanks — please include suggested SLA and cost estimate for 1-slot reservation.

mike_oncall: summary for thread: likely noisy-tenant long-context causing KV cache thrash -> p99 regressions. Immediate mitigations applied (concurrency cap, long-request 429, reserved slot + prefetch tweak). Next steps: follow-up perf graphs, customer trial of reserved capacity, consider heap tuning and increasing caching window for embeddings runtime.

omar_cust: can we get a timeline for when reserved trial can be scheduled? aiming for next nightly window (04:00 UTC tomorrow).

jess_support: I'll coordinate trial slot tomorrow and loop in billing for short-term pro-rate.

mike_oncall: OK locking in trial for next night. If anything regresses reopen thread. :thumbsup:
